## 432. The present on causal-set growth (UE14)

UE, a unified explanation of reality, names presence in time among its structural gaps: the grammar has no relation of presence in time, and adding one is a choice of model ([plan](../../development/ue-unified-explanation/PLAN.md#5-the-structural-gaps); 01's open entry). UE13 read causal set theory and its classical sequential growth on the root and on processes ([§431](431.md#431-precedence-and-its-links-what-can-be-born-next-against-what-continues-ue13)), a model in which the question can be asked exactly: the past is held and the labels, the order of births, carry no physical meaning. UE14 reads the present at a stage of a course as the maximal elements of what it has born, and asks which relations of presence every course growing a configuration keeps and which some course has ([note](../../development/ue14-the-present/NOTE.md)).

**Its standing.** Every law is near-definitional, a lemma, a witness or a calibration. The natural labellings of a finite order are its linear extensions, connected by exchanging adjacent incomparable elements (Mazurkiewicz's traces, here an instance of the core's theorem); a finite order is the intersection of its linear extensions (Szpilrajn 1930; Dushnik and Miller 1941); the prefixes of linear extensions are the down-sets, here the stems with decided membership, Brightwell and others' characterization of their stem sets (2003), here on finite causal sets; every antichain is the set of maximal elements of its down-closure. The bounds on presence at a birth (a covering pair; the one upper cover) and on being present together (incomparable; the same strict up-set) are elementary consequences, not found stated in the sources read. The calibrations are lemmas of their laws: agreement across all courses settles that one element conditions another, or that two share their future, only up to double negation, and asserting it is deciding whether it does; finding a course that bears two unrelated elements in either order, or shows a link present at a birth, is deciding for each pair only whether its precedence fails. The stable partition is the one new construction, counting with no pigeonhole. What is new is the reading: these as the covariant content of presence on the growth, the answer in this model to 01's open entry for one reading of presence, the exact decisions, and Wüthrich and Callender's relation on the diamond as the past joined with being present together on every course.

It found the prose saying more than the Lean in six places, in 18 findings (2 errors, 4 over- or understatements, 7 improvements, 5 on naming or style), and every one is taken ([note §7](../../development/ue14-the-present/NOTE.md#7-review)). The decision was misplaced: presence on every course read as the one link needs none, and the laws on some course need precedence only weakly decided, each decision now calibrated exactly. Dowker's present is a birth. What every course keeps is defined from precedence rather than being a relation of precedence, since being present together on every course relates elements neither of which precedes the other. Wüthrich and Callender's relation is the join on their four elements, and a witness off them shows that the join need not be their relation and need not be transitive. Stein's conclusion is a maximum here, not a uniqueness, and the stages are the stems with decided membership. The orders of birth became one theorem (natural_iff_course); OnFrontier became MaximalBorn, since the core's frontier is that of a comparison among alternatives, Through became LeastAbove, Natural NaturalLabelling and Related Comparable. The fold had 147 theorems in 173 declarations; the course forms, added after the review so that the laws read on every or some course are stated on the courses and connect to the base, bring it to 163 theorems in 189 declarations. **Decisions at landing.** One module, one record, homed at 01 §1 after precedence and its links: the question it answers is the root's open entry on presence in time, and 01's open entry is narrowed to it, keeping open presence on the theory's other models, continuous time, the present of a center and weighted growths. The record depends on precedence-and-its-links for `Causet` and the links, on what-can-be-born-next for stems, courses and relabelling, on normal-forms-need-decided-apartness and order-of-exchanges-is-the-invariant for the core's arrangements, on continuation-relative-to-a-class for the grammar's ending, and on counts-exist-where-decided for deciding. Being present together is not the root's co-presence, 俱有, mutual reach, which no two elements of a causal set have; the names say "together" for it. The calibrations are stated as equivalences with excluded middle and its weak form, each with what the need says about the unfolding. `count` is kept local rather than importing `Becoming.Frequency`, which would add six modules to the leaf's closure. **Readings** [AI reading, D45]. In this model the root's open question has an answer for each reading of presence. Read as being in the configuration, a condition once born is still there when what it conditions is born, on every course, since the past is held; read as Dowker's present, the birth, or as a maximal antichain of the configuration, it is not, whatever the course. Read as being among the maximal elements of what has been born, the answer varies with the course between two bounds that do not: it can be present exactly where it conditions what is born directly, and must be exactly where that is the one thing it conditions directly. Being born before and being present together go the same way. Whatever every course keeps, or some course has, is defined from precedence; some of it goes beyond precedence itself, since being present together on every course relates elements neither of which precedes the other, and a relation read on one course, a present at a stage or a foliation, is a choice of course. So, given covariance, a premise of the model, the grammar's condition relation defines every relation of presence the growth keeps, and its lack of a primitive relation of presence in time loses no covariant content here; the entry stays open for the theory's other models, continuous time, the present of a center and growths whose courses are weighted. Wüthrich and Callender find Stein's theorem false for a single causal set, since invariance under the automorphisms of one configuration admits a relation beyond the past; they grant a local becoming defined from the causal order, which past_every_iff reads on courses as the largest relation every course respects, leaving their negative result standing, and on their four elements their relation adds to the past being present together on every course. The continuation condition's future, read as what a thing conditions under any class given on the elements, is the same on every course, and read as what comes after a present stage, or under a class given on the order of births, it is a choice of course; this bears on scope, not on order, which stays with calling widening better (C).
